SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.34
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by strong aliphatic C-H stretches at 2878, 2932 and 2963 cm⁻¹ and a deformation band at 1453 cm⁻¹, indicating a saturated, highly-branched hydrocarbon skeleton.  A characteristic cluster of Raman bands for a 1,3-dioxolane ring appears at 825–960 cm⁻¹ (ring breathing / C–O–C stretches) and at 1044–1140 cm⁻¹ (ring C–O stretches).  The experimental peaks 825, 872, 957, 1044 and 1137 cm⁻¹ match these typical dioxolane modes (literature: ring breathing 845-880 cm⁻¹; ν(C-O-C) 950 cm⁻¹; coupled C–O stretches 1035-1150 cm⁻¹).  Among the candidates, only molecule 4 (CCC(C)C1OCC1O) contains a 1,3-dioxolane ring attached to a branched isopropyl group, providing both the ring signatures and the strong aliphatic bands observed.  Other candidates lack the dioxolane ring (1,2,6,8,10) or possess nitro/azide groups (3) that would give additional high-frequency bands not seen.  Therefore candidate 4 offers the best structural fit to the full Raman pattern.
